QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/10/2026 19:36 in a 78-year-old woman. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s, coefficient of variation 0.16, pNN50 0.55) with no organised P activity, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 136 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +8 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at about 140 bpm with QTc 430 ms, so there is no interval change; both contradict the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which is raised separately as a documentation conflict.

12-lead of 8/2/2025 in an 84-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.86-0.88 s) with a P before each QRS, PR 160 ms; QRS narrow at 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -22 degrees, within the normal range. QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 was also sinus (60 bpm, QRS 76 ms, QTc 394 ms) but with reversed-looking limb leads (negative P-QRS-T in I with positive aVR); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged, so no change categories apply.

12-lead of 5/23/2024, the only ECG for this 58-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +9 degrees (normal). QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 12/25/2025, the only ECG for this 57-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (RR 0.82-0.84 s), PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +23 degrees (normal). QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms - not prolonged. It predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, which is why the post-start ECG requirement is recorded separately as overdue.

12-lead of 11/15/2024, two days after aortic valve replacement, in a 64-year-old woman with known atrial fibrillation. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.69-1.16 s, coefficient of variation 0.20, pNN50 0.62) with no organised P waves (lead II atrial deflection 0.045 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of about 61 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +30 degrees (normal). QT 457 ms, Bazett QTc about 462 ms on the mean RR. The pre-operative ECG of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves (PR 180 ms) and QTc 393 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; the QTc change is below 60 ms.

12-lead of 3/9/2025 in a 51-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +63 degrees (normal). QT 415 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was essentially the same (sinus 62 bpm, QTc 433 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This remains her most recent tracing and predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

12-lead of 8/23/2025, the only ECG for this 61-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (RR 0.72-0.73 s), PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/19/2020 in a 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT 426 ms, Bazett QTc 481 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms, and she takes no QT watch-list drug. The prior ECG of 2/2/2020 was also sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 512 ms; the QTc fell by about 31 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold, and there is no rhythm or conduction change.

12-lead of 1/18/2021. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, variability minimal), consistent P waves with PR about 180 ms, QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +44 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 98 ms, QTc 426 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and the QTc change is only about 33 ms, below the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 6/23/2025 in a 48-year-old man. Regular sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a P wave before each QRS; PR is at the upper limit of normal at about 195 ms, not enough for first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +49 degrees (normal). QT 389 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms at RR 1.10 s. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was also sinus bradycardia (51 bpm, PR about 192 ms, QTc 352 ms), so nothing has changed.

12-lead of 9/13/2025 07:17, the morning of cardiac surgery, in a 60-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 9/11/2025. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.29-0.58 s, coefficient of variation 0.19, pNN50 0.61) with no P waves at all in lead II (0.012 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 151 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -9 degrees (normal). QT 247 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 18:57 showed sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with clear P waves (PR about 150 ms) after one early beat, and QTc 405 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; telemetry confirmed AF on 9/13 and 9/15/2025.

12-lead of 11/23/2025 in a 55-year-old woman, matching the same-day note describing sinus rhythm. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with a P before each QRS, PR 172 ms; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +10 degrees (normal). QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a much longer QT (494 ms, QTc 523 ms), so the QTc has fallen by about 138 ms - a decrease of 60 ms or more - with no change in rhythm or conduction.

12-lead of 10/8/2023, the most recent tracing for this 56-year-old man on escitalopram. Regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, P before each QRS with PR 128 ms, QRS 88 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT is clearly long at 484 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 516 ms at RR 0.88 s. Versus the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 356 ms) the QTc has increased by about 160 ms, far beyond 60 ms, which is why a QT safety review item has also been raised.

12-lead of 4/19/2024, the only ECG for this 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with consistent P waves, PR 136 ms, QRS 86 ms and no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +72 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 410-440 ms, not prolonged for the rate. No prior tracing available for comparison.

12-lead of 8/23/2021 10:07, recorded about one minute after the prior tracing. Regular sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 84 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal), QT 316 ms with Bazett QTc 412 ms. The immediately preceding ECG of 8/23/2021 10:06 was essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 407 ms); no new rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

12-lead of 10/24/2024 in an 80-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin. Despite the AF history this tracing shows sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 182 ms) and almost no RR variability; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal), QT 427 ms and Bazett QTc 397 ms at RR 1.16 s. The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm, QTc 387 ms) with one interpolated ectopic beat, so there is no new AF, no new block and no significant QTc change.

12-lead of 12/5/2024 14:38. Low-amplitude but regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 0.49 s, coefficient of variation 0.002) with P waves preceding each QRS, PR about 186 ms. QRS has narrowed to 92 ms with no terminal delay, and the frontal axis is about +73 degrees (normal, though low voltage makes this approximate). QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. The earlier tracing the same morning (106516875, 01:33) showed a 152 ms QRS with an rSR' in V1 peaking at 112 ms and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, so the block was transient/rate-related. QTc fell by about 43 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 11/24/2025 in a 79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started. Rhythm is sinus at 62 bpm (regular, RR 0.94-0.98 s) with a P before each QRS, PR 172 ms; QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal). The QT is markedly long at 528 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 537 ms. Compared with the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has risen by about 127 ms, well over 60 ms - the basis for the accompanying QT safety item.

12-lead of 9/17/2024, the day after coronary bypass grafting, and the only ECG for this 60-year-old man with atrial fibrillation. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.29, pNN50 0.73) with no discernible P waves (lead II atrial deflection only 0.05 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101 bpm; there is therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS is narrow at 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -33 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms using the mean RR. No prior ECG for comparison; telemetry also showed AF on 9/19-9/20/2024.

items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed 3/14/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (female 1, age 65-74 1, essential hypertension 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, score >=2). Her current regimen (famotidine, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID, levothyroxine; last renewed 6/23/2026) contains no anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant appears in any cardiology clinic note through 6/23/2026. Needs prescriber review for starting anticoagulation.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/15/2026 valid to 1/7/2027, continuously prescribed since 2023). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QT 486 ms and Bazett QTc 525 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Citalopram at 40 mg exceeds the dose usually advised when QTc is prolonged; prescriber review is required.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/18/2026 valid to 12/26/2026, continuous since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, and 160 ms longer than the 11/23/2022 tracing (QTc 356 ms); the 5/14/2024 note describing that ECG as having an acceptable QT understates it. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026). Prescriber review is required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025; it was absent from the 9/21/2025 medication list and first ordered that day. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met within the required time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026 (first order for this patient, listed as a new medication in that note). The start was before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window, due 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026 (QTc 464 ms), within the window, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026 (first citalopram order; the 12/15/2025 note listed warfarin only). Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc 374 ms), within the window, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and therefore outside the required window; no qualifying tracing exists and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the 2/18/2026 list; the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (no outpatient escitalopram since brief 2024 orders), so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG exists in the chart. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026; her only prior exposure was inpatient in February-March 2025. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but as of the 9/24/2026 review the due date has not yet passed, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window, so the monitoring requirement was met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 6/22/2026) list persistent atrial fibrillation, with continuous telemetry-documented AF 1/17-1/20/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1) so anticoagulation is strongly recommended. Dabigatran was stopped during the January 2025 admission and never restarted: current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only (orders of 6/22/2026). Needs review for restarting anticoagulation.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue in this 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation diagnosed 8/22/2025 (carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note, most recently 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis 1), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. He has never been started on one: current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg only (order 6/27/2026); tamsulosin was stopped 6/27/2026. A peri-procedural haemorrhage was coded in August 2025 but no ongoing bleeding risk is documented. Needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation listed in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 8/4/2026) and telemetry-documented AF 2/26-3/3/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy 1, essential hypertension 1); for a man with a score of 2 the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. His current outpatient orders (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) contain no anticoagulant even though long-term anticoagulant use was coded during the June 2025 admission. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as current and re-ordered (valid to 1/4/2027), alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented reason it should not continue without review; the requested cardiology decision on resuming apixaban after the bleed has not been documented.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was also ordered (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); the note itself lists both drugs in the current medication list. In a patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and CLL this duplication carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 140 bpm with no discernible P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day and telemetry showed AF on 6/10-6/12/2026. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart needs correction.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 6/17/2026 valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 554 ms and Bazett QTc 543 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, both acceptable, so drug effect rather than electrolytes is the likely driver. She also takes metoprolol succinate and warfarin.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/12/2026 valid to 1/9/2027). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QT 528 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, and a rise of about 125 ms from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 410 ms). Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms at RR 0.74 s - well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold despite citalopram. Confirms the same-day note describing sinus rhythm; no prior ECG for comparison.

Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, both acceptable, so drug effect rather than electrolytes is the likely driver. She also takes metoprolol succinate and warfarin.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/12/2026 valid to 1/9/2027). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QT 528 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, and a rise of about 125 ms from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 410 ms). interpretations.explanation: 12-lead of 3/7/2026, the only ECG in this 66-year-old man's chart. Regular sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright P before every QRS in II/aVF (PR 184 ms), narrow QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms at RR 0.74 s - well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold despite citalopram. Confirms the same-day note describing sinus rhythm; no prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 7/15/2025 in a 48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and cardiomyopathy. This tracing is regular (RR 0.57-0.59 s, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a discrete P wave before each QRS, so it is sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm and not AF; PR is short at about 130 ms. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT 328 ms with Bazett QTc about 431 ms; the T wave is broad and low so this estimate is approximate. The prior ECG of 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc about 418 ms, so no new arrhythmia, no new block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

12-lead of 5/21/2024, the only ECG for this 47-year-old man. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, essentially regular (RR 0.54-0.62 s), with a P wave before each QRS; PR is about 130 ms although the preceding T wave partly fuses with the P at this rate. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/10/2026 19:36 in a 78-year-old woman. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s, coefficient of variation 0.16, pNN50 0.55) with no organised P activity, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 136 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +8 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at about 140 bpm with QTc 430 ms, so there is no interval change; both contradict the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which is raised separately as a documentation conflict.

12-lead of 8/2/2025 in an 84-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.86-0.88 s) with a P before each QRS, PR 160 ms; QRS narrow at 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -22 degrees, within the normal range. QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 was also sinus (60 bpm, QRS 76 ms, QTc 394 ms) but with reversed-looking limb leads (negative P-QRS-T in I with positive aVR); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged, so no change categories apply.

12-lead of 5/23/2024, the only ECG for this 58-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +9 degrees (normal). QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 12/25/2025, the only ECG for this 57-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (RR 0.82-0.84 s), PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +23 degrees (normal). QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms - not prolonged. It predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, which is why the post-start ECG requirement is recorded separately as overdue.

12-lead of 11/15/2024, two days after aortic valve replacement, in a 64-year-old woman with known atrial fibrillation. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.69-1.16 s, coefficient of variation 0.20, pNN50 0.62) with no organised P waves (lead II atrial deflection 0.045 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of about 61 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +30 degrees (normal). QT 457 ms, Bazett QTc about 462 ms on the mean RR. The pre-operative ECG of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves (PR 180 ms) and QTc 393 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; the QTc change is below 60 ms.

12-lead of 3/9/2025 in a 51-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +63 degrees (normal). QT 415 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was essentially the same (sinus 62 bpm, QTc 433 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This remains her most recent tracing and predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

12-lead of 8/23/2025, the only ECG for this 61-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (RR 0.72-0.73 s), PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/19/2020 in a 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT 426 ms, Bazett QTc 481 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms, and she takes no QT watch-list drug. The prior ECG of 2/2/2020 was also sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 512 ms; the QTc fell by about 31 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold, and there is no rhythm or conduction change.

12-lead of 1/18/2021. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, variability minimal), consistent P waves with PR about 180 ms, QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +44 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 98 ms, QTc 426 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and the QTc change is only about 33 ms, below the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 6/23/2025 in a 48-year-old man. Regular sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a P wave before each QRS; PR is at the upper limit of normal at about 195 ms, not enough for first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +49 degrees (normal). QT 389 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms at RR 1.10 s. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was also sinus bradycardia (51 bpm, PR about 192 ms, QTc 352 ms), so nothing has changed.

12-lead of 9/13/2025 07:17, the morning of cardiac surgery, in a 60-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 9/11/2025. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.29-0.58 s, coefficient of variation 0.19, pNN50 0.61) with no P waves at all in lead II (0.012 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 151 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -9 degrees (normal). QT 247 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 18:57 showed sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with clear P waves (PR about 150 ms) after one early beat, and QTc 405 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; telemetry confirmed AF on 9/13 and 9/15/2025.

12-lead of 11/23/2025 in a 55-year-old woman, matching the same-day note describing sinus rhythm. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with a P before each QRS, PR 172 ms; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +10 degrees (normal). QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a much longer QT (494 ms, QTc 523 ms), so the QTc has fallen by about 138 ms - a decrease of 60 ms or more - with no change in rhythm or conduction.

12-lead of 2/15/2025, the only ECG for this 64-year-old woman. QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/26/2023 in a 70-year-old man with atrial flutter in his history. This tracing is strictly regular (RR 0.536-0.540 s) with a discrete P wave before each QRS and no sawtooth atrial activity, so it is sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm rather than flutter; PR 164 ms. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +42 degrees (normal). QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was nearly identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QTc 404 ms), so there is no change.

12-lead of 10/8/2023, the most recent tracing for this 56-year-old man on escitalopram. Regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, P before each QRS with PR 128 ms, QRS 88 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT is clearly long at 484 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 516 ms at RR 0.88 s. Versus the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 356 ms) the QTc has increased by about 160 ms, far beyond 60 ms, which is why a QT safety review item has also been raised.

12-lead of 4/19/2024, the only ECG for this 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with consistent P waves, PR 136 ms, QRS 86 ms and no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +72 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 410-440 ms, not prolonged for the rate. No prior tracing available for comparison.

12-lead of 8/23/2021 10:07, recorded about one minute after the prior tracing. Regular sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 84 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal), QT 316 ms with Bazett QTc 412 ms. The immediately preceding ECG of 8/23/2021 10:06 was essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 407 ms); no new rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

12-lead of 10/24/2024 in an 80-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin. Despite the AF history this tracing shows sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 182 ms) and almost no RR variability; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal), QT 427 ms and Bazett QTc 397 ms at RR 1.16 s. The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm, QTc 387 ms) with one interpolated ectopic beat, so there is no new AF, no new block and no significant QTc change.

12-lead of 12/5/2024 14:38. Low-amplitude but regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 0.49 s, coefficient of variation 0.002) with P waves preceding each QRS, PR about 186 ms. QRS has narrowed to 92 ms with no terminal delay, and the frontal axis is about +73 degrees (normal, though low voltage makes this approximate). QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. The earlier tracing the same morning (106516875, 01:33) showed a 152 ms QRS with an rSR' in V1 peaking at 112 ms and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, so the block was transient/rate-related. QTc fell by about 43 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 11/24/2025 in a 79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started. Rhythm is sinus at 62 bpm (regular, RR 0.94-0.98 s) with a P before each QRS, PR 172 ms; QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal). The QT is markedly long at 528 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 537 ms. Compared with the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has risen by about 127 ms, well over 60 ms - the basis for the accompanying QT safety item.

12-lead of 9/17/2024, the day after coronary bypass grafting, and the only ECG for this 60-year-old man with atrial fibrillation. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.29, pNN50 0.73) with no discernible P waves (lead II atrial deflection only 0.05 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101 bpm; there is therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS is narrow at 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -33 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms using the mean RR. No prior ECG for comparison; telemetry also showed AF on 9/19-9/20/2024.

items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed 3/14/2025. Needs prescriber review for starting anticoagulation.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026 (first citalopram order; the 12/15/2025 note listed warfarin only). Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc 374 ms), within the window, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and therefore outside the required window; no qualifying tracing exists and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the 2/18/2026 list; the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (no outpatient escitalopram since brief 2024 orders), so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG exists in the chart. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026; her only prior exposure was inpatient in February-March 2025. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but as of the 9/24/2026 review the due date has not yet passed, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window, so the monitoring requirement was met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 6/22/2026) list persistent atrial fibrillation, with continuous telemetry-documented AF 1/17-1/20/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1) so anticoagulation is strongly recommended. Dabigatran was stopped during the January 2025 admission and never restarted: current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only (orders of 6/22/2026). Needs review for restarting anticoagulation.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue in this 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation diagnosed 8/22/2025 (carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note, most recently 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis 1), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. He has never been started on one: current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg only (order 6/27/2026); tamsulosin was stopped 6/27/2026. A peri-procedural haemorrhage was coded in August 2025 but no ongoing bleeding risk is documented. Needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation listed in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 8/4/2026) and telemetry-documented AF 2/26-3/3/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy 1, essential hypertension 1); for a man with a score of 2 the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. His current outpatient orders (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) contain no anticoagulant even though long-term anticoagulant use was coded during the June 2025 admission. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as current and re-ordered (valid to 1/4/2027), alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented reason it should not continue without review; the requested cardiology decision on resuming apixaban after the bleed has not been documented.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was also ordered (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); the note itself lists both drugs in the current medication list. In a patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and CLL this duplication carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 140 bpm with no discernible P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day and telemetry showed AF on 6/10-6/12/2026. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart needs correction.

The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm, QTc 387 ms) with one interpolated ectopic beat, so there is no new AF, no new block and no significant QTc change.

12-lead of 12/5/2024 14:38. Low-amplitude but regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 0.49 s, coefficient of variation 0.002) with P waves preceding each QRS, PR about 186 ms. QRS has narrowed to 92 ms with no terminal delay, and the frontal axis is about +73 degrees (normal, though low voltage makes this approximate). QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. The earlier tracing the same morning (106516875, 01:33) showed a 152 ms QRS with an rSR' in V1 peaking at 112 ms and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, so the block was transient/rate-related. QTc fell by about 43 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 11/24/2025 in a 79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started. Compared with the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has risen by about 127 ms, well over 60 ms - the basis for the accompanying QT safety item.

Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 140 bpm with no discernible P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day and telemetry showed AF on 6/10-6/12/2026. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart needs correction.

12-lead of 8/2/2025 in an 84-year-old woman. QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 was also sinus (60 bpm, QRS 76 ms, QTc 394 ms) but with reversed-looking limb leads (negative P-QRS-T in I with positive aVR); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged, so no change categories apply.

12-lead of 5/23/2024, the only ECG for this 58-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +9 degrees (normal). QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 12/25/2025, the only ECG for this 57-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (RR 0.82-0.84 s), PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +23 degrees (normal). QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms - not prolonged. It predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, which is why the post-start ECG requirement is recorded separately as overdue.

12-lead of 11/15/2024, two days after aortic valve replacement, in a 64-year-old woman with known atrial fibrillation. 12-lead of 3/9/2025 in a 51-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +63 degrees (normal). QT 415 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was essentially the same (sinus 62 bpm, QTc 433 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This remains her most recent tracing and predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

12-lead of 8/23/2025, the only ECG for this 61-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (RR 0.72-0.73 s), PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/19/2020 in a 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). 12-lead of 1/18/2021. 12-lead of 11/23/2025 in a 55-year-old woman, matching the same-day note describing sinus rhythm. Precordial leads are normal. QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms - not prolonged despite escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

interpretations.explanation: 12-lead of 3/7/2026, the only ECG in this 66-year-old man's chart. QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms at RR 0.74 s - well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold despite citalopram. Confirms the same-day note describing sinus rhythm; no prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 7/15/2025 in a 48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and cardiomyopathy. This tracing is regular (RR 0.57-0.59 s, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a discrete P wave before each QRS, so it is sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm and not AF; PR is short at about 130 ms. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT 328 ms with Bazett QTc about 431 ms; the T wave is broad and low so this estimate is approximate. The prior ECG of 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc about 418 ms, so no new arrhythmia, no new block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

12-lead of 5/21/2024, the only ECG for this 47-year-old man. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, essentially regular (RR 0.54-0.62 s), with a P wave before each QRS; PR is about 130 ms although the preceding T wave partly fuses with the P at this rate. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/10/2026 19:36 in a 78-year-old woman. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s, coefficient of variation 0.16, pNN50 0.55) with no organised P activity, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 136 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +8 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at about 140 bpm with QTc 430 ms, so there is no interval change; both contradict the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which is raised separately as a documentation conflict.

12-lead of 8/2/2025 in an 84-year-old woman. QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 was also sinus (60 bpm, QRS 76 ms, QTc 394 ms) but with reversed-looking limb leads (negative P-QRS-T in I with positive aVR); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged, so no change categories apply.

12-lead of 5/23/2024, the only ECG for this 58-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +9 degrees (normal). QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 12/25/2025, the only ECG for this 57-year-old woman. 12-lead of 3/9/2025 in a 51-year-old woman. 12-lead of 1/18/2021. 12-lead of 11/23/2025 in a 55-year-old woman, matching the same-day note describing sinus rhythm. 12-lead of 6/26/2023 in a 70-year-old man with atrial flutter in his history. 12-lead of 3/14/2025, the only ECG for this 71-year-old woman, recorded the day paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was diagnosed. 12-lead of 4/29/2026, the only ECG for this 42-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, P before each QRS with PR 154 ms; QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane QRS is negative in I, II and aVF and positive in aVR, giving a measured axis of about -173 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (north-west) quadrant; this pattern is also typical of left/right arm lead reversal and should be confirmed with a repeat tracing. Precordial leads are normal. QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms - not prolonged despite escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 10/8/2023, the most recent tracing for this 56-year-old man on escitalopram. Regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, P before each QRS with PR 128 ms, QRS 88 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 410-440 ms, not prolonged for the rate. No prior tracing available for comparison.

12-lead of 8/23/2021 10:07, recorded about one minute after the prior tracing. QTc fell by about 43 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

Compared with the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has risen by about 127 ms, well over 60 ms - the basis for the accompanying QT safety item.

Precordial leads are normal. QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms - not prolonged despite escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

interpretations.explanation: 12-lead of 3/7/2026, the only ECG in this 66-year-old man's chart. Regular sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with an upright P before every QRS in II/aVF (PR 184 ms), narrow QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms at RR 0.74 s - well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold despite citalopram. Confirms the same-day note describing sinus rhythm; no prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 7/15/2025 in a 48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and cardiomyopathy. This tracing is regular (RR 0.57-0.59 s, coefficient of variation 0.01) with a discrete P wave before each QRS, so it is sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm and not AF; PR is short at about 130 ms. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT 328 ms with Bazett QTc about 431 ms; the T wave is broad and low so this estimate is approximate. The prior ECG of 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc about 418 ms, so no new arrhythmia, no new block and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

12-lead of 5/21/2024, the only ECG for this 47-year-old man. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm, essentially regular (RR 0.54-0.62 s), with a P wave before each QRS; PR is about 130 ms although the preceding T wave partly fuses with the P at this rate. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT 324 ms, Bazett QTc 438 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/10/2026 19:36 in a 78-year-old woman. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s, coefficient of variation 0.16, pNN50 0.55) with no organised P activity, i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 136 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +8 degrees (normal). QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 413 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at about 140 bpm with QTc 430 ms, so there is no interval change; both contradict the 6/10/2026 clinic note describing sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, which is raised separately as a documentation conflict.

12-lead of 8/2/2025 in an 84-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.86-0.88 s) with a P before each QRS, PR 160 ms; QRS narrow at 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -22 degrees, within the normal range. QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 was also sinus (60 bpm, QRS 76 ms, QTc 394 ms) but with reversed-looking limb leads (negative P-QRS-T in I with positive aVR); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged, so no change categories apply.

12-lead of 5/23/2024, the only ECG for this 58-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 97 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +9 degrees (normal). QT 332 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 12/25/2025, the only ECG for this 57-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 72 bpm (RR 0.82-0.84 s), PR 140 ms, QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +23 degrees (normal). QT 372 ms, Bazett QTc 408 ms - not prolonged. It predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, which is why the post-start ECG requirement is recorded separately as overdue.

12-lead of 11/15/2024, two days after aortic valve replacement, in a 64-year-old woman with known atrial fibrillation. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.69-1.16 s, coefficient of variation 0.20, pNN50 0.62) with no organised P waves (lead II atrial deflection 0.045 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of about 61 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +30 degrees (normal). QT 457 ms, Bazett QTc about 462 ms on the mean RR. The pre-operative ECG of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves (PR 180 ms) and QTc 393 ms, so this represents new atrial fibrillation; the QTc change is below 60 ms.

12-lead of 3/9/2025 in a 51-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a P before each QRS and a short PR of about 112 ms; QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +63 degrees (normal). QT 415 ms, Bazett QTc 409 ms. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was essentially the same (sinus 62 bpm, QTc 433 ms), so no rhythm, conduction or QTc change. This remains her most recent tracing and predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

12-lead of 8/23/2025, the only ECG for this 61-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 83 bpm (RR 0.72-0.73 s), PR 152 ms, QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). QT 336 ms, Bazett QTc 396 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/19/2020 in a 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 66 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT 426 ms, Bazett QTc 481 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms, and she takes no QT watch-list drug. The prior ECG of 2/2/2020 was also sinus at 75 bpm with QTc 512 ms; the QTc fell by about 31 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold, and there is no rhythm or conduction change.

12-lead of 1/18/2021. Regular sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm (RR 0.50 s, variability minimal), consistent P waves with PR about 180 ms, QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +44 degrees (normal). QT 278 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, QRS 98 ms, QTc 426 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no new conduction block and the QTc change is only about 33 ms, below the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 6/23/2025 in a 48-year-old man. Regular sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a P wave before each QRS; PR is at the upper limit of normal at about 195 ms, not enough for first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +49 degrees (normal). QT 389 ms, Bazett QTc 370 ms at RR 1.10 s. The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was also sinus bradycardia (51 bpm, PR about 192 ms, QTc 352 ms), so nothing has changed.

12-lead of 9/13/2025 07:17, the morning of cardiac surgery, in a 60-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded 9/11/2025. The ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 0.29-0.58 s, coefficient of variation 0.19, pNN50 0.61) with no P waves at all in lead II (0.012 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation with a rapid mean ventricular rate of about 151 bpm; no measurable PR interval. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -9 degrees (normal). QT 247 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms on the mean RR. The prior tracing of 9/12/2025 18:57 showed sinus rhythm at about 77 bpm with clear P waves (PR about 150 ms) after one early beat, and QTc 405 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; telemetry confirmed AF on 9/13 and 9/15/2025.

12-lead of 11/23/2025 in a 55-year-old woman, matching the same-day note describing sinus rhythm. Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with a P before each QRS, PR 172 ms; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +10 degrees (normal). QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 showed sinus rhythm at 67 bpm with a much longer QT (494 ms, QTc 523 ms), so the QTc has fallen by about 138 ms - a decrease of 60 ms or more - with no change in rhythm or conduction.

12-lead of 2/15/2025, the only ECG for this 64-year-old woman. Regular sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.80-0.84 s) with a low-amplitude but reproducible P wave before each QRS, PR about 168 ms; QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal). QT 376 ms, Bazett QTc 418 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 6/26/2023 in a 70-year-old man with atrial flutter in his history. This tracing is strictly regular (RR 0.536-0.540 s) with a discrete P wave before each QRS and no sawtooth atrial activity, so it is sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm rather than flutter; PR 164 ms. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +42 degrees (normal). QT 294 ms, Bazett QTc 401 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was nearly identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, QRS 94 ms, QTc 404 ms), so there is no change.

12-lead of 3/14/2025, the only ECG for this 71-year-old woman, recorded the day paroxysmal atrial fibrillation was diagnosed. The underlying rhythm is sinus at about 61 bpm: RR intervals are 0.96-0.99 s apart from a single premature beat at 0.54 s followed by a compensatory pause of 1.36 s, and a reproducible P wave precedes each sinus QRS with PR about 190 ms - this is sinus rhythm with one ectopic beat rather than atrial fibrillation. QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -24 degrees (normal). QT 381 ms, Bazett QTc 385 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 4/29/2026, the only ECG for this 42-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, P before each QRS with PR 154 ms; QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane QRS is negative in I, II and aVF and positive in aVR, giving a measured axis of about -173 degrees, i.e. in the extreme (north-west) quadrant; this pattern is also typical of left/right arm lead reversal and should be confirmed with a repeat tracing. Precordial leads are normal. QT 348 ms, Bazett QTc 374 ms - not prolonged despite escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 11/10/2023, the most recent tracing for this 35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg. Regular sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with a P before each QRS, PR 154 ms; QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +52 degrees (normal). The T wave is broad and late: QT 486 ms with a Bazett QTc of 525 ms, above the 500 ms watch-list threshold, which is raised as a separate QT safety item. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 133 bpm with QTc about 512 ms, so the QTc change is only about 13 ms and no change category applies.

12-lead of 3/8/2026, the only ECG for this 44-year-old man and the study obtained after escitalopram was started on 2/12/2026. Regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 142 ms, QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). QT 436 ms, Bazett QTc 464 ms - mildly prolonged but below the 500 ms threshold, so no QT safety item is required, although repeat surveillance is reasonable. No prior ECG for comparison.

12-lead of 1/13/2019 in a 74-year-old man. Regular sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm with a P before each QRS, PR 182 ms; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -12 degrees (normal). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 348 ms at RR 1.14 s. The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 was also sinus (66 bpm, QRS 104 ms, PR 208 ms, QTc 385 ms); QRS has if anything narrowed, so there is no new block and the QTc change is under 60 ms.

12-lead of 10/8/2023, the most recent tracing for this 56-year-old man on escitalopram. Regular sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, P before each QRS with PR 128 ms, QRS 88 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +50 degrees (normal). QT is clearly long at 484 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 516 ms at RR 0.88 s. Versus the prior ECG of 11/23/2022 (sinus 75 bpm, QTc 356 ms) the QTc has increased by about 160 ms, far beyond 60 ms, which is why a QT safety review item has also been raised.

12-lead of 7/13/2022 in a 61-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter and a pacemaker. This tracing is strictly regular (RR 0.40-0.45 s, coefficient of variation 0.02) and a reproducible low-amplitude P wave precedes every QRS with PR about 160 ms; there is one atrial deflection per ventricular beat and no 2:1 sawtooth, so this is sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm, not flutter, and there are no pacing spikes (intrinsic narrow QRS 80 ms, no bundle branch block). Frontal axis about 0 degrees (normal). QT 264 ms, Bazett QTc 405 ms. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 0.38-0.82 s, coefficient of variation 0.24, no P waves) at about 105 bpm with QTc 421 ms, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved; the QTc change is under 60 ms.

12-lead of 5/12/2025, the only ECG for this 71-year-old man. Regular sinus rhythm at 82 bpm (RR 0.71-0.74 s) with a low-amplitude P wave before each QRS, PR about 145 ms; QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +26 degrees (normal). QT 361 ms, Bazett QTc 423 ms. No prior tracing for comparison.

12-lead of 4/19/2024, the only ECG for this 53-year-old woman. Regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with consistent P waves, PR 136 ms, QRS 86 ms and no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +72 degrees (normal). QT 289 ms, Bazett QTc 410-440 ms, not prolonged for the rate. No prior tracing available for comparison.

12-lead of 8/23/2021 10:07, recorded about one minute after the prior tracing. Regular sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 84 ms without bundle branch block, frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal), QT 316 ms with Bazett QTc 412 ms. The immediately preceding ECG of 8/23/2021 10:06 was essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, QRS 84 ms, QTc 407 ms); no new rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

12-lead of 10/24/2024 in an 80-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin. Despite the AF history this tracing shows sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a P wave before every QRS (PR 182 ms) and almost no RR variability; QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal), QT 427 ms and Bazett QTc 397 ms at RR 1.16 s. The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm, QTc 387 ms) with one interpolated ectopic beat, so there is no new AF, no new block and no significant QTc change.

12-lead of 12/5/2024 14:38. Low-amplitude but regular sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 0.49 s, coefficient of variation 0.002) with P waves preceding each QRS, PR about 186 ms. QRS has narrowed to 92 ms with no terminal delay, and the frontal axis is about +73 degrees (normal, though low voltage makes this approximate). QT 296 ms, Bazett QTc 421 ms. The earlier tracing the same morning (106516875, 01:33) showed a 152 ms QRS with an rSR' in V1 peaking at 112 ms and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, so the block was transient/rate-related. QTc fell by about 43 ms, less than the 60 ms threshold.

12-lead of 11/24/2025 in a 79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started. Rhythm is sinus at 62 bpm (regular, RR 0.94-0.98 s) with a P before each QRS, PR 172 ms; QRS 94 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +59 degrees (normal). The QT is markedly long at 528 ms giving a Bazett QTc of 537 ms. Compared with the pre-amiodarone ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, QTc 410 ms) the QTc has risen by about 127 ms, well over 60 ms - the basis for the accompanying QT safety item.

12-lead of 9/17/2024, the day after coronary bypass grafting, and the only ECG for this 60-year-old man with atrial fibrillation. The rhythm is irregularly irregular (RR 0.39-1.07 s, coefficient of variation 0.29, pNN50 0.73) with no discernible P waves (lead II atrial deflection only 0.05 mV), i.e. atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 101 bpm; there is therefore no measurable PR interval. QRS is narrow at 76 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -33 degrees, i.e. left axis deviation. QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 417 ms using the mean RR. No prior ECG for comparison; telemetry also showed AF on 9/19-9/20/2024.

items.explanation: 71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation diagnosed 3/14/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (female 1, age 65-74 1, essential hypertension 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline, score >=2). Her current regimen (famotidine, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg BID, levothyroxine; last renewed 6/23/2026) contains no anticoagulant, and no anticoagulant appears in any cardiology clinic note through 6/23/2026. Needs prescriber review for starting anticoagulation.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/15/2026 valid to 1/7/2027, continuously prescribed since 2023). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QT 486 ms and Bazett QTc 525 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. Citalopram at 40 mg exceeds the dose usually advised when QTc is prolonged; prescriber review is required.

56-year-old man on escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/18/2026 valid to 12/26/2026, continuous since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT 484 ms and Bazett QTc 516 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, and 160 ms longer than the 11/23/2022 tracing (QTc 356 ms); the 5/14/2024 note describing that ECG as having an acceptable QT understates it. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (3/18/2026). Prescriber review is required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025; it was absent from the 9/21/2025 medication list and first ordered that day. Because the start was on or after 9/1/2025 and before 3/1/2026 the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due within 30 days, i.e. by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met within the required time.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026 (first order for this patient, listed as a new medication in that note). The start was before 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo applies with a 30-day window, due 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded 3/8/2026 (QTc 464 ms), within the window, so the requirement was met.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026 (first citalopram order; the 12/15/2025 note listed warfarin only). Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc 374 ms), within the window, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. The only ECG in the chart (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and therefore outside the required window; no qualifying tracing exists and the due date has passed, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026 (it was not on the 2/18/2026 list; the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026 (no outpatient escitalopram since brief 2024 orders), so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. The telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - but the report was requested by fax and has not been received, and no ECG exists in the chart. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026; her only prior exposure was inpatient in February-March 2025. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since 3/9/2025, but as of the 9/24/2026 review the due date has not yet passed, so the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/1/2026 Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, within the window, so the monitoring requirement was met.

80-year-old woman whose cardiology clinic notes (most recently 6/22/2026) list persistent atrial fibrillation, with continuous telemetry-documented AF 1/17-1/20/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI 1, female 1) so anticoagulation is strongly recommended. Dabigatran was stopped during the January 2025 admission and never restarted: current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only (orders of 6/22/2026). Needs review for restarting anticoagulation.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits. Under the 3/1/2026 memo a confirmatory INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The last INR in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the requirement is overdue in this 95-year-old on concurrent amiodarone.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation diagnosed 8/22/2025 (carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note, most recently 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis 1), so oral anticoagulation is recommended. He has never been started on one: current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg only (order 6/27/2026); tamsulosin was stopped 6/27/2026. A peri-procedural haemorrhage was coded in August 2025 but no ongoing bleeding risk is documented. Needs prescriber review.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation listed in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 8/4/2026) and telemetry-documented AF 2/26-3/3/2025. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure/acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy 1, essential hypertension 1); for a man with a score of 2 the guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. His current outpatient orders (famotidine, pantoprazole, sertraline) contain no anticoagulant even though long-term anticoagulant use was coded during the June 2025 admission. Needs prescriber review.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. At the 8/20/2026 cardiology clinic visit apixaban 5 mg twice daily was nevertheless listed as current and re-ordered (valid to 1/4/2027), alongside aspirin and clopidogrel. The anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented reason it should not continue without review; the requested cardiology decision on resuming apixaban after the bleed has not been documented.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was also ordered (valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); the note itself lists both drugs in the current medication list. In a patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and CLL this duplication carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 140 bpm with no discernible P waves, i.e. atrial fibrillation; unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded that day and telemetry showed AF on 6/10-6/12/2026. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the same-day tracings and the chart needs correction.

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 6/17/2026 valid to 1/6/2027). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 554 ms and Bazett QTc 543 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (6/17/2026) are potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL, both acceptable, so drug effect rather than electrolytes is the likely driver. She also takes metoprolol succinate and warfarin.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/12/2026 valid to 1/9/2027). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025, obtained two weeks after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm, QT 528 ms, Bazett QTc 537 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document, and a rise of about 125 ms from the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025 (QTc 410 ms). Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.
